headline: Revenue growth and cost cuts flip operations to profit
summary_short: nCino's FY2026 Q2 revenue was $159.4M (+10.6% y/y), gross profit $100.9M (+16.8% y/y), and operations swung to a $21.1M profit from a $1.5M loss a year ago; net income attributable to nCino reached $13.6M versus $5.6M a year ago.
summary_long: Subscription revenue grew 12.2% y/y to $140.9M (88.4% of revenue): 72.6% of the increase came from existing-customer expansion, 27.4% from new customers. Gross margin rose to 63.3% from 60.0% as revenue outgrew cost of revenue. Opex fell on the prior workforce reduction: R&D -$4.5M (headcount -92), G&A -$4.4M, while S&M rose only $0.8M on higher commissions — swinging operating income to +$21.1M from a $1.5M loss. Net income rose to $13.6M from $5.6M, helped by a lower effective tax rate (10.1% vs 43.0%) despite a $16.4M FX-driven swing in other income/expense. Cash was $102.8M; a new $200M term loan partly funded $110.5M of buybacks this quarter. RPO was $1.3B.

drivers.explanation: Subscription-led revenue growth combined with lower R&D and G&A headcount costs following the prior-year workforce reduction swung operations from a loss to a $21.1M profit.
Subscription revenue growth: 72.6% from expansion within existing customers, 27.4% from new customers who didn't contribute a year ago; professional services revenue was essentially flat.
Gross margin rose to 63.3% from 60.0% because revenue grew 10.6% y/y while cost of revenue grew only modestly (subscription cost +$3.1M, professional-services cost -$2.3M).
R&D expense fell $4.5M (headcount -92) and G&A fell $4.4M (headcount -19) from the prior workforce reduction, while S&M rose only $0.8M on higher commission expense.

Aided by a lower effective tax rate (10.1% vs 43.0%, attributed to valuation-allowance and profitability changes), partly offset by a $16.4M y/y swing in other income/expense from intercompany-loan FX settlements.
Tracks the net income increase against a lower weighted diluted share count (109.5M vs 116.6M a year ago) after this quarter's buybacks.
